name: Vallée de la Marne

known.via: English Wikipedia "Vallée de la Marne" (a wine place on Wikidata)

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Most Champagne is non-vintage, a blend of several years for a steady house style. In great years a house may declare a vintage and bottle wine from that harvest alone.
Made only from white grapes. In Champagne that usually means 100% Chardonnay.
White wine made only from black grapes. In Champagne, Pinot Noir, Meunier or both.
How sweet a sparkling wine is after dosage: Extra Brut under 6 g of sugar a liter, Brut under 12, Demi-sec 32 to 50. Brut is the most common.

notes: Pinot Noir gives Champagne body and structure, Chardonnay brings freshness, and Meunier adds roundness.
Most Champagne is non-vintage. Houses blend grapes, villages and reserve wines from earlier years to keep the same style every year.
White Champagne can be made from black grapes, because gentle pressing keeps the color out of the juice.
A dosage of sugar and wine sets the sweetness, and today it is used mostly to fine-tune the sense of acidity.

blurb.text: A Champagne sub-region along the Marne, with more variable soils than the other sub-regions. It has only two Grands Crus villages, Aÿ and Tours-sur-Marne.
